summary.en: After many verbs you must learn which pattern follows. Some take the **-ing form** (_enjoy_, _avoid_, _suggest_, _finish_, _keep_), others the **to-infinitive** (_decide_, _hope_, _manage_, _refuse_, _afford_), and some take an object first (_She asked me to wait_). After a **preposition**, always use -ing: _interested in learning_.
summary.es: En español casi siempre usamos el infinitivo («disfruto leyendo», «decidí ir»). En inglés, tras enjoy, avoid, suggest o finish va -ing, y tras decide, hope o refuse va to + infinitivo. Hay que aprender cada verbo.

form: Verb + **-ing**: _enjoy, avoid, suggest, finish, keep, mind, practise, consider, imagine_
Verb + **to-infinitive**: _decide, hope, manage, plan, refuse, afford, agree, promise, seem_
Verb + object + **to-infinitive**: _ask, tell, want, allow, advise, persuade_
Modal verbs and _let/make_ + object take the **bare infinitive**: _She made me wait._
Preposition + **-ing**: _good at cooking, instead of going, before leaving_
Purpose: **to + infinitive**: _I came to ask for help._

uses.text: **Verbs followed by -ing**: _I **avoid driving** in the city centre._
**Verbs followed by to-infinitive**: _They **decided to move** abroad._

note.en: Say want me to do, not want that I do.
note.es: No se dice want that I do: es want me to do.

uses.text: **Purpose with to**: _I'm saving money **to buy** a flat._ Don't use for + -ing for purpose.

mistakes.wrong: I enjoy to read at night.

why.en: Enjoy is followed by the -ing form, never by to + infinitive.
why.es: Tras enjoy va -ing, aunque en español usemos infinitivo.

mistakes.wrong: He suggested to go by train.

why.en: Suggest takes -ing (or a that-clause), not to-infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: I want that you help me.
mistakes.right: I want you to help me.

why.en: After want, use object + to-infinitive, not a that-clause.
why.es: «Quiero que me ayudes» es I want you to help me.

mistakes.wrong: I'm looking forward to see you.
mistakes.right: I'm looking forward to seeing you.

why.en: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so it takes -ing.
why.es: En look forward to, to es preposición: va -ing.

mistakes.wrong: She went to the shop for buying bread.
mistakes.right: She went to the shop to buy bread.

why.en: Purpose is expressed with to + infinitive.
why.es: Para expresar finalidad («para comprar») usa to + infinitivo, no for + -ing.

examples.en: She finished writing the report before lunch.
examples.es: Terminó de escribir el informe antes de comer.

examples.en: We can't afford to buy a bigger flat.
examples.es: No podemos permitirnos comprar un piso más grande.

examples.en: He refused to answer any questions.
examples.es: Se negó a responder a ninguna pregunta.

examples.en: I'd avoid travelling on Friday evening if I were you.
My manager allowed me to work from home.
Do you mind opening the window a little?
They managed to catch the last train.
Instead of complaining, why don't you speak to him?
He promised to call as soon as he landed.

explanation.en: Decide is followed by the to-infinitive.

practice.prompt: Would you mind ___ the music down a bit?

explanation.en: Mind is followed by the -ing form.

practice.prompt: She's very good at ___ people to relax.

explanation.en: After a preposition (at), we use the -ing form.

practice.prompt: Our teacher advised us ___ the text twice.
